newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium prices slide with LME.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium prices slide with LME.

text.p: Taiwan's aluminium ingots prices fell to T$47.50 per kg from T$49.00 two weeks ago, reflecting a recent decline in aluminium prices on the London Metal Exchange, metals traders said on Tuesday.
"The aluminium ingots prices are following the world trend because the local demand has yet to pick up," a local metal trader said.

Taiwan traders have predicted local demand for basic metals to pick up slowly as the government's economy stimulus plans take effect on the construction industry, which remains Taiwan's top sector for basic metals consumption.

Loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 9.99 percent to T$392.833 billion in February from a year ago, marking the 21st consecuctive month of declines, Taiwan central bank figures showed.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has been in deep recession since the local property market peaked in 1989.
In August 1996, the central bank scrapped all selective credit controls on land to boost the property market and economy, and analysts had expected the move to gradually take effect.
Taiwan's copper wire and strip prices also dropped to reflect recent falling world copper prices.
